entries.definition: Let p:E→C and p′:E′→C be functors. A strict isomorphism over C is a functor H:E→E′ such that p′H=p and with a strictly inverse functor H⁻¹:E′→E satisfying HH⁻¹=id_{E′} and H⁻¹H=id_E (hence pH⁻¹=p′). It is stronger than an equivalence of categories over C.

entries.definition: Let L/K be a field extension and α∈L. Multiplication by α defines a K-linear endomorphism m_α:L→L by m_α(x)=αx. When L/K is finite, its determinant is the field norm N_{L/K}(α); without finite dimensionality this determinant is not generally defined.

entries.context: Real analysis · interval between endpoints, possibly infinite
entries.definition: For extended-real endpoints −∞≤a<b≤+∞, the open interval (a,b) is the set {x∈ℝ:a<x<b}; infinite endpoints impose no finite upper or lower bound. With a<b it is nonempty, and (−∞,+∞)=ℝ. An empty interval may arise if the endpoint inequality is dropped, but is excluded by this stated convention.

entries.context: Field theory · fractions of a polynomial ring in indeterminates
entries.definition: For a field k and a set I of algebraically independent formal indeterminates (X_i)_{i∈I}, the rational function field k(X_i:i∈I) is the fraction field of the integral domain k[X_i:i∈I]. Every element can be represented by f/g with f,g polynomials and g≠0, and therefore depends on finitely many indeterminates.

entries.term: fibre category over a base object
entries.context: Category theory · fibre of a functor over an object

entries.term: relative diagonal of a scheme morphism
entries.context: Algebraic geometry · diagonal X→X×_S X
entries.definition: For a morphism of schemes f:X→S, the relative diagonal Δ_{X/S}:X→X×_S X is the unique morphism with both compositions with the two projections equal to id_X. entries.context: Category theory · both initial and terminal object
entries.definition: An object 0 of a category C is a zero object if it is both initial and terminal: for every X∈C there is exactly one arrow 0→X and exactly one arrow X→0. When a zero object exists, the composites X→0→Y define zero morphisms; the object is unique up to unique isomorphism.

entries.context: Probability · integrability of the kth absolute power
entries.definition: For a real-valued random variable X and real k>0, the kth absolute moment is E[|X|^k]=∫|X|^k dP, valued in [0,∞]. The kth absolute moment is called finite when this integral is less than ∞; equivalently |X|^k is integrable. For k=0 the usual convention gives E[1]=1 on a probability space, including at X=0 by defining |X|⁰=1.

entries.context: Ring theory · element with a zero power
entries.definition: An element x of an associative ring R is nilpotent if x^n=0 for some positive integer n. The exponent may depend on x. In a nonzero ring the multiplicative identity 1 is not nilpotent; in the zero ring it is, because 1=0.
